- Section Eight: Safe Driving","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C - Section Eight: Safe Driving

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Map the zones: green ahead, blue beside, yellow blind spots, red behind; keep eyes moving with scans ten seconds ahead to buy reaction time and dodge last-second moves [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Tailgating blinds and compresses reactions, so hold three seconds, lift off when cut off, and widen gaps for tailgaters behind by holding course then merging right, plus room behind bikes on metal and gravel [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A02
Mind the flanks: shun others' blind spots, never pace alongside, open room for freeway mergers even holding priority, space off parked cars, and look both ways even facing red lights and stop signs [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A02
Blind spots sit beside and slightly behind the driver; check with shoulder glances that move only the head before lane changes, turns, merges, backing, departures, parking moves, curb pullouts, and door openings [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A03
Rear checks defeat rear-enders: sweep mirrors and turn the head when changing lanes, checking blinds, slowing, turning into drives, parking, working curbs, and backing [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A03
Run high beams on dark open roads while stopping inside the lit stretch, dim for oncoming traffic, and when blinded look right or aside without retaliating; rain means low beams never parking lights alone [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A03
Night walkers, riders, and work zones demand extra care and slower speeds, eyes need adjustment time leaving bright places, and single approaching lights demand a far-right berth for bikes, motos, or dead lamps [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A04
Fight glare with clean glass, polarized shades, roomy gaps, a working visor, pedestrian watchfulness, and avoiding sunrise and sunset runs [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A04
Skids mean lost traction; ice and snow skid hardest when fast or downhill, so slow early for curves, shun fast turns and stops, drop gears before descents, dodge slick patches, and in a skid lift off, skip brakes, steer into it, seek dry pavement [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A05
Locked skids follow hard fast braking; four-wheel ABS takes firm pressure, rear ABS eases to rolling then steers into the skid, front ABS releases and straightens, ABS-less cars pump, sunk pedals pump gently with downshifts and emergency brakes, wet brakes dry under gas plus brake [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A05
Wet roads cut five to ten miles per hour, packed snow halves speed, ice caps at five; shade hides ice that freezes first and dries last, bridges freeze first, and first rain on dry oily pavement demands instant slowing [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A06
Storms cap sight near one hundred feet and speed at thirty; run wipers, low beams, and defroster, clear mud and snow off glass and lights, and carry correct chains in snow country [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A06
Hydroplaning floats the car on water with zero road contact, so slight inputs trigger spins; prevent with slow speeds, water dodging, slosh heeding, and gentle lane moves, and when floating ease off without touching brakes [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A06
Escape snow and mud with low gears and straight wheels, gentle unsprung gas, forward-reverse rocking to freedom, and boards or branches under the tires only while stopped [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A07
Floods threaten sweep-off, debris, collapse, breakdowns, and electrocution with unreadable depths; deep water means rerouting, forced crossings go slow, and brakes get tested right after [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A07
High winds menace tall rigs most; slow down, grip firmly, watch for debris, shun cruise control, and pull over to wait out the worst [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A08
Fog and smoke favor postponement; forced trips go slow on low beams never parking lights, stop inside sight distance, widen gaps, wipe and defog, hold lanes, listen for hidden traffic, and pull off with flashers when too thick [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A08
Traffic breaks weave patrol lights to clear hazards, fog jams, and crash risks; drivers flash along, match the officer's gentle pace at distance, and never pass until lights die and conditions clear [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A09
Belts bind everyone with tickets for skippers and drivers answering for unbelted under-sixteens; crash physics keeps bodies flying at travel speed into glass and across seats, belts holding position and softening blows [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A09
Belt right: shoulder strap snug across chest never under arms or behind backs, lap belt low on hips against submarining, pregnancy routing the lap low under the belly and the strap between breasts past the bulge [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A10
Kids ride approved restraints by size: under two, forty pounds, three-four height ride rear-facing never before airbags; under eight or four-nine ride restrained in back with narrow front exceptions; eight or four-nine graduates to standard belts, installs checked by pros [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A11
Airbags assist belts; drivers and passengers sit ten inches off the covers measured chest to wheel, dealers advising the cramped, and children beside side bags face grave risk [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A11
Never leave six-and-under alone in cars with supervisors twelve-plus required, and never cook kids or animals in hot parked cars whose heat spikes even on cracked windows toward dehydration, heatstroke, and death [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A11
The Basic Speed Law bans speeds unsafe for conditions regardless of signs, weighing traffic, surfaces, walkers, weather, and congestion without freeway weaving; defaults cap at sixty-five on highways, fifty-five on two-lane roads and while towing [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A12
Split dangers by severity: bike versus oncoming means slowing, yielding the lane to the car, then passing the bike with three feet or using the left lane against steady flows [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A12
Blowouts forbid panic braking or lifting; grip with both hands, hold speed while safe, ease off the gas, steer straight to stabilize, look where you want to go, then slow and pull off [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A12
Pavement departures need a firm grip, foot off gas, gentle braking, a rear check, and a careful reentry, never violent yanks toward oncoming traffic [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A13
Heat waves demand gauge watching, no sustained speeding, and air conditioning off; cold snaps demand gauge watching for antifreeze gaps plus defrosting or cracked windows, manuals holding details [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A13
Freeway failures pull fully right, exit and reenter from the right, call five-eleven or find a box, return quickly, stay belted inside with flashers as needed, abandoning the car only for missing shoulders, guardrails, or true refuges [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A13
Commute-hour freeway patrols give free gas gallons, jumps, radiator patches, flat changes, crash reports, and free tows to approved spots when dead, refusing private tows, shop tips, motorcycles, and crashes unless directed, all via five-eleven [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A14
Trapped on tracks facing a train with flashers: exit instantly, run diagonally away toward the train's origin side, then call emergency services [A14].
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A14
Trapped with no train or flashers: exit, call the posted crossing number with the crossing ID to report the car, then call emergency services [A14].
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A14
Distraction kills through phones, navigation, kids, pets, music, and grooming; handheld use is illegal, adults go hands-free only when needed, calls wait for voicemail or pullouts, texts and emails wait always [A14].
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A15
Mount phones on glass, dash, or console clear of sight lines for single-swipe use only; minors face a total wireless ban behind the wheel except emergency calls [A15].
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A15
Assistance systems and self-drivers react non-humanly, so expect alien responses to road events [A15].
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A15
Carbon monoxide kills odorlessly from exhaust pipes, so never idle in closed garages; tiredness, yawning, dizziness, nausea, headaches, and ringing ears all demand an exhaust check [A15].
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]
